Seminar Title:

Synthesis and characterization of Ba2Zn2Fe12O22-MFe2O4 (M=Zn, Co, Ni, Mg) ferrite composite for high-frequency antenna application.

Seminar Type:

Synopsis Seminar

Department:

Ceramic Engineering

Student

Abstract:

Abstract: In the present study, Y-type hexaferrite&ndashspinel ferrite composites with the general composition (Ba₂Zn₂Fe₁₂O₂₂)₁₋ₓ(MFe₂O₄)ₓ (M = Co, Ni, Zn, Mg x = 0.0&ndash1.0) were successfully synthesized using the coprecipitation method. Structural analysis through X-ray diffraction confirmed the coexistence of hexagonal ferrite Ba₂Zn₂Fe₁₂O₂₂ (Zn₂Y) and spinel (MF) ferrite phases without the formation of any impurity phases. Microstructural investigations revealed an improved densification of x = 0.2 compositions in all composites. The systematic incorporation of spinel ferrites significantly influenced the magnetic, dielectric, and electromagnetic properties of the composites.

Zn₂Y&ndashCoF composites showed permittivity (&epsilon) in the range 14 to 31 and permeability (&micro) in the range 13-18 at 100 MHz. These composites demonstrated stable permittivity and permeability up to 500 MHz. Among all composition, &nbspx= 0.4 composition demonstrated a high miniaturization factor (n) &asymp 14, characteristic impedance (Zi) &asymp 1, and outstanding antenna performance with a return loss of &minus36 dB and VSWR &asymp 1 at 7.6 GHz.

Similarly, Zn₂Y&ndashNiF composites exhibited &epsilon in the range 13-28 and &micro in the range 17-21 at 100 MHz. Among all composition, (Zn₂Y)₀.₆(NiF)₀.₄ demonstrated a high miniaturization factor (n = 19.2), characteristic impedance (Zi = 1.1), and outstanding antenna performance with a reflection loss of &minus43.8 dB and VSWR &asymp 1 at 5 GHz, confirming an excellent impedance matching and radiation efficiency.

Zn₂Y&ndashZnF composites showed e in the range 18-24 and &micro in the range 15&ndash20 and stable electromagnetic response up to 500 MHz with low losses. Among all composition, x = 0.4 composition demonstrated strong antenna performance with a return loss of &minus33 dB at 8.44 GHz, a wide bandwidth of approximately 0.95 GHz, and VSWR &asymp 1, making it suitable for broadband X-band applications.

Furthermore, Zn₂Y&ndashMgF composites showed e in the range 10-20 and &micro in the range 25&ndash30. Among all composition, x = 0.4 composition achieved excellent antenna performance with a return loss of &minus43 dB at around 6 GHz, a bandwidth of approximately 0.96 GHz, and VSWR &asymp 1, indicating superior impedance matching and efficiency.

Overall, the study demonstrates that (Zn₂Y)₀.₆(MgF)₀.₄ and (Zn₂Y)₀.₆(NiF)₀.₄ composites exhibit a desirable balance of dielectric and magnetic properties, leading to enhanced magneto-dielectric coupling and improved antenna characteristics.
